audits.text:
## 40f6e5fa30e1

**Reproduced exact-override defect; no fix made.** Generator SHA-256
`c47efe5874558d5adbbfe61197fb36ee22be01b3da8eabb714e630d928aecb2c`
advertises exact controls including `n_dual_touch`, `n_decor`, and
`n_single_1`, but generation uses independent random counts rather than those
requested values.

At seed `314`, sample index `7`, difficulty `medium`, I compared boundary
requests `n_dual_touch=1` versus `5`, `n_decor=0` versus `4`, and
`n_single_1=0` versus `4`. All six calls returned the byte-identical grid SHA-256
`8b779b11697179196989c709f530cd3bb1ed50936ebe3377ff668a849c7d08c7`.
Every grid passes `self_check`, but all have the same observed counts: four
dual-touch zero cells, one decor cell, and fourteen single-touch zero cells.
The exact six cases and grids are in
`checks/audit/40f6e5fa30e1/override-reproducer.json`. A retained replay script
regenerated all six calls from the pinned source, found one unique grid hash,
and reported zero mismatches in
`checks/audit/40f6e5fa30e1/replay-result.json`.

The official exhaustive override stage was started, but the external command
window interrupted it before a receipt or finished aggregate; its retained
`result.json` still says `status: running`. I do **not** claim that stage passed
or completed. The direct six-call reproducer is sufficient for the specific
ignored-axis finding. I left the audit target unchanged.

triage.reason: Accepted as reviewer-reported, source-bound findings: 9e0cd377fa63 omits NE-SW corner-pair coverage and its submitted lawful witness exposes an authority mismatch; 40f6e5fa30e1 ignores exact count controls. Both audited hashes match live source and both remain unapproved. The interrupted exhaustive override wrapper is not a completed check; manual reproducer evidence is retained. No audit-target approval or repair is inferred.
